changes.before: Reuse a name field in a scored record.
changes.after: Reuse an object's required fields and add another one.

before: An interface describes an object shape. TimedItem extends NamedItem means a TimedItem must have NamedItem’s title property as well as its own minutes property. extends here combines checked descriptions; it does not copy runtime data or create a class inheritance relationship.

A value containing only minutes is not a TimedItem because title is still required. An extension also cannot replace title:string with an incompatible title:number. The child description must stay compatible with its parent’s requirements.

Define NamedRecord with title:string, then define ScoredRecord extending it with score:number. Implement scoredLabel(record: ScoredRecord): string to return title, a colon and space, then score. Equivalent safe structural types are acceptable to the public compiler checks; the lesson demonstrates extends as one reuse tool.
after: An interface describes an object's shape. Extends lets one interface keep another interface's requirements and add more. It does not copy actual data or create objects.
Leaving out title still causes an error. An extending interface also cannot replace a required text title with an incompatible numeric title.
Define NamedRecord with a string title. Extend it with a numeric score in ScoredRecord. Make scoredLabel return the title, a colon and space, then the score.

before.question: A TimedItem object has minutes:12 but no title. Why is it rejected?
choices: The extended interface still requires the parent’s title field.
Interfaces create title automatically at runtime.
before.explanation: Extending reuses the parent requirements and adds new ones. It does not fill missing data.

after.question: Why is a TimedItem with minutes but no title rejected?
choices: The parent's title is still required
after.explanation: Extending adds requirements while keeping the existing ones.
